chunks: Muḥammad ibn Qays narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

If the owned mukātab stipulates with his master that no wala' will be due from him to anyone, or if the master stipulates the wala' of the mukātab and the mukātab who was contracted agrees, then his wala' belongs to him.

He said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled concerning a mukātab upon whom his wala' had been stipulated when he was emancipated. He married a bondwoman belonging to another man, and she bore him a child. Then his child was freed. Then the mukātab died, and his child inherited from him. Then they differed concerning his child as to who would inherit him, so he attached his child to the mawālī of his father.

key_terms.السَّيِّدُ: The master who holds authority in the manumission contract.
key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبُ: A slave under a manumission contract.
key_terms.مَوَالِي أَبِيهِ: The patrons/mawālī affiliated with his father.
key_terms.مَوْلَاهُ: His master or patron in the legal relationship of ownership and wala'.
key_terms.وَلَاءَ: The legal bond of clientage and inheritance affiliation connected to emancipation.

ai.seo_question: How is wala' determined for a mukātab, and who inherits through that affiliation after emancipation?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal consequences of stipulating wala' in the contract of a mukātab, affirming that such a condition is effective when accepted. It also records a judicial ruling of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning inheritance and affiliation through the father's mawālī after emancipation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3488 - Muhammad ibn Qays narrated from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), who said:

"If a mukatab (a slave under a contract of emancipation) stipulates with his master that there will be no wala' (loyalty) upon him, or if the master stipulates that the wala' of the mukatab will belong to him and the mukatab agrees, then the wala' belongs to the master."

Imam (as) said: "Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, ruled regarding a mukatab who had a condition in his contract that his wala' would belong to his master upon his emancipation. The mukatab married a bondwoman belonging to another man, and she bore him a child. The child was then freed.
Later, the mukatab died, and his child inherited from him.
There was a dispute regarding who would inherit from the child. Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, ruled that the child should be affiliated with the master of his father."
